Flow.description: Portal flow (Screen Flow: Business License Application Facility). The Facility Application on the portal, for a threading or alternative hair design facility. The applicant (the owner) gives the facility type, opening date, the facility's name, phone, addresses, parish and tax identification number, reads the equipment list and requirements printed for that type, may upload their local occupational license, and certifies that everyone working there is licensed or permitted. Their operator's license is checked by the inspector, not uploaded. On certifying it creates the establishment (a business Account, Establishment record type, with the applicant related as Owner), a submitted Business License Application (New Establishment, License Type Threading Facility or Alternative Hair Design Facility) and the inspection and license fees from the Fee Schedule, paid by check or money order to the inspector. Keeps a draft until certify, so it can be saved for later for 30 days. Runs in system context; it only uses the signed-in applicant's own records. Staff can also enter it for an applicant from New Application on the Person Account (input recordId); the pay step then tells them to record the payment.

fields.name: RQ_Threading
fields.fieldText:
Threading Facilities

Threading is the only service allowed in a threading facility. Threading shall not be performed in any threading facility or salon unless the following items are available for use:

1. Hand washing sink; 2. hot and cold running water; 3. stool for operator and chair for client; 4. lamp; 5. sanitizers or sterilizers for implements; 6. blood spill kit; 7. thread; 8. towels; 9. covered waste bins; 10. covered container for towels; 11. first aid kit; and 12. Gold Book (rule book).

Threading Facility Requirements

1. Submit a completed facility application along with required fees and documentation. 2. Adhere to all safety and sanitation requirements of L.A.C. 46:XXXI.700(A-R) which are applicable to a threading facility. 3. Certify that all persons employed and/or performing services are appropriately licensed by this board. 4. Provide only services that fall within the scope of threading as defined in L.A.C. 46:XXXI.1110 (A). 5. A threading facility owner, who is not a licensed cosmetologist or an esthetician or permitted as a threader, shall employ one or more registered managers who shall be licensed as cosmetologists or estheticians or permitted as a threader. A registered manager shall be present at the facility during all hours of operation and shall be responsible for ensuring that all persons practicing threading within the facility are appropriately licensed and follow all applicable laws and rules and regulations. A threading facility owner who is absent from his respective facility more than two working days per week shall employ a manager, who shall be a registered cosmetologist or an esthetician or a permitted threader and who shall obtain a certificate of registration as a manager.

fields.name: RQ_Ahd
fields.fieldText:
Alternative Hair Design Facility (AHD)

Alternative hair design services are the only services allowed in an alternative hair design facility. Alternative hair design (AHD) services shall not be performed in any facility or salon unless the following items are available for use or displayed:

1. At least one sign with lettering of at least 3 inches that states "NO CHEMICAL SERVICES ALLOWED"; 2. One or more shampoo bowl(s) with hot and cold running water and an adjustable chair; 3. An operational restroom with a sink for hand washing with hot and cold running water; 4. At least 1 heat resistant braiding bib for every operator providing the applicable service; 5. Kettle (for dipping braids); 6. One large sanitation center or a wet and dry sanitizer at each station; 7. One or more hair dryer(s) and a blow dryer; 8. Workstation for each operator with adequate workspace for tools and product; 9. One enclosed and labeled storage area for clean towels; 10. One covered and labeled container for soiled towels; 11. One covered and labeled trash container maintained in a sanitary manner; 12. Blood spill kit; 13. First aid kit; 14. Gold Book.

AHD Facility Requirements

1. Submit a completed facility application along with required fees and documentation to the inspector. 2. Adhere to all safety and sanitation requirements of L.A.C. 46:XXXI.700(A-R). 3. Certify that all persons employed and/or performing services are appropriately license/permitted by this board. There shall be no training in the facility. 4. Provide only services that fall within the scope of AHD as defined in L.A.C. 46:XXXI.101 (A). 5. An AHD owner shall be a registered cosmetologist, a current holder of an AHD permit, or owner shall employ a manager that is either a cosmetologist or a current holder of an AHD permit and obtain a certificate of registration as a manager. A registered manager shall be present at the facility during all hours of operation and shall be responsible for ensuring that all persons practicing AHD within the facility are appropriately licensed/permitted and follow all applicable laws, rules and regulations. Also, an AHD facility owner who is absent from his respective facility more than two working days per week shall employ a manager, who shall be a registered cosmetologist or hold an AHD permit and who shall obtain a certificate of registration as a manager.
